summary: ACCEPT after three rounds, with one REQUIRED follow-up test named below. Every defect is measured-fixed by EXECUTION, not by reading. NEW-1 fixed: the notified-marker is now nested inside PYTHON_EXIT==0 AND report_complete, proven by an identical three-tick one-variable pair - the mutant latches on a MISSING push at T1 and never delivers the day's real numbers, while HEAD delivers them at T3. Crash retries and preserves eod_failed_*; --force writes only a scratch artifact, never the canonical path, and never sets the marker; an ntfy HTTP 500 is detected, logged and retried; a normal success latches and the second tick is a clean no-op. ⭐ ADOPTION FIDELITY RESTORED AND PROVEN: the split is back - a22e9440 is the byte adoption (wrapper only, +27 lines) and 3d2b3f38 the harden - and git show a22e9440:ops/health/eod_cron.sh hashes exactly 380f1fc825e9f8b1e671cdfc25a5722b135cd72f915cc50d6a8b3064297da8c5, the box file. The provenance now lives in the ADOPTION COMMIT BODY and the tautological three-constant test is removed, which is a better home than I proposed. Installer ownership corrected to -o trader -g trader, matching both siblings; it fails closed on non-root, missing or non-executable eod_counts.py, a crontab not referencing the target, and absent ntfy config, all before any mutation; exec bits committed 100755. set -euo pipefail correctly REJECTED and the reason stated - it would make a crash silent. Guard exits now emit distinct [EOD-CRON-SKIPPED] reasons, so a weekend is no longer byte-identical to a crash. ⛔ REQUIRED FOLLOW-UP, one test: the mutant reverting the latch to file-existence SURVIVES, and it is NOT equivalent - seeding a partial canonical report, exactly what the adopted script produced at a22e9440:19, makes the mutant push an empty verdict line forever while HEAD regenerates and delivers. Add a test that seeds a partial canonical and asserts the real report is produced. Accepted rather than blocked because the head code is proven correct on that path and the gap is a future-regression guard, on an ops-only PR that restarts no service. ⛔ RESIDUAL for the handoff, out of scope here: if cron itself never fires - crond dead, crontab lost, box down - there is still ZERO evidence anywhere. The heartbeat proves observability only WHEN the wrapper runs; from the ntfy channel a dead cron and a weekend remain indistinguishable. That needs a separate watchdog. NIT: the PR body says 6 focused controls; the file has 7.
